source.label: In a model of prime sums at one height: a point rightmost in the whole configuration shows on a window of lengths unless the other points near its height carry a weighted count of at least its multiplicity; a progression that hides; the link to weighted prime sums

reviewer: Claude Code proof assessment; fresh medium reviewer

claims.summary: W >= 0 integrable on [0, l], not almost everywhere zero, a(z) = int W(v) e^(zv) dv; Z a multiset of points rho = beta + i gamma with multiplicities m_rho >= 1, tau real, sum over Z of m_rho |a(rho - i tau)| e^(beta_rho u) finite at the two ends of each window used; P(u) = sum m_rho a(rho - i tau) e^((rho - i tau) u). (1) If rho_0 = beta_0 + i tau is in Z with multiplicity m_0, every point has beta_rho <= beta_0, U1 real, R > 0 and |P(u)| <= E(u) on [U1, U1 + R], then m_0 <= sup over the window of E(u) e^(-beta_0 u)/a(beta_0) + sum over the other points of m_rho e^(-(beta_0 - beta_rho) U1) min(1, 16/(R^2 (gamma_rho - tau)^2)). (2) If moreover U1 >= 0 and, for some eta > 0 and g > 0, the other points with beta_rho > beta_0 - eta have multiplicities at most m' and heights gamma with |gamma - tau| >= g and pairwise distances at least g, and the remaining points have at most kappa log(|t| + 3) of them, with multiplicity, in each |gamma - t| <= 1, then m_0 <= sup E(u) e^(-beta_0 u)/a(beta_0) + (16 pi^2/3) m'/(R g)^2 + kappa e^(-eta U1) [log(|tau| + 3) + (32/R^2)(1.645 log(|tau| + 4) + 1.9)]. (3) For W continuous on the line, supported in [0, l], and the points beta_0 + i(tau + j g), j an integer, unit multiplicities, with a(beta_0 + i lambda) = O(1/lambda^2): P(u) = (2 pi/g) sum over integers n of W(2 pi n/g - u) e^(2 pi n beta_0/g), which is 0 on every window [U1, U1 + R] with no multiple of 2 pi/g in [U1, U1 + R + l]. (4) Under the premise of the Riesz mean formula from one premise, for W the hat function on [0, l] and tau real with i tau not a zero: sum over n of Lambda(n) n^(-i tau) W(log n - u) = a(1 - i tau) e^((1 - i tau) u) - P(u) - sum over q >= 1 of a(-2q - i tau) e^(-(2q + i tau) u) for u > 0, P taken over the nontrivial zeros.
claims.assessment: Working elementary proof of (1) to (3): P is averaged against a triangle on the window after division by the rightmost point's exponential, whose transform at a point with real part at most 0 is at most min(1, 16/(R^2 lambda^2)) in modulus, and |a(beta + i lambda)| <= a(beta) <= a(beta_0) for a nonnegative weight on v >= 0; (2) is (1) with a sum over separated heights and a shell count; (3) is Poisson summation, the transport to a continuous weight of the progression named in the fourteenth route review for the sharp cutoff. The mechanism is that of the short resonance-free range, a recorded theorem in the Gram model, carried to prime sums at one height with a pointwise premise. Part (4) is the second difference in the length of the Riesz mean formula and is conditional on that formula's premise. Numerical control: (3) on a truncated progression; (1) in 200 random configurations, a weak check of the direction only, the constants never binding; no instance computed for (2). For exact hiding at equal real parts and unit multiplicities, (2) excludes R g > 7.26 and (3) realises R g < 2 pi - l g.
claims.rationale: Answers in part the fourteenth review's test on Turan's line, in a model: a point rightmost in the whole configuration shows on a window of lengths unless near-tied points stand closer in height than about 7.3 divided by the window's logarithmic length; the bound uses the near-tied points' largest multiplicity and a local count of the lower points. An arithmetic progression of spacing below 2 pi over that length hides exactly. For points closer than that and not in progression nothing is proved; an unverified construction of the reviewer suggests about kappa log tau of them can hide.
claims.next_action: Verify or break the reviewer's construction of close points that hide a strictly rightmost one.
claims.formalization_scope: Not formalized; no Lean work assigned.

notes.mathematical_status: Complete proof of (1) to (3) in the entry with a numerical control of (1) and (3); (4) conditional on the registered formula's premise.
notes.significance: Context: a model statement on one conditional line of the route; the mechanism is on record in another setting. No novelty claimed.
notes.relationships: Carries the mechanism of the short resonance-free range to Turan's setting; replaces the margin of the margin-rightmost zero count by a separation in height, for a premise on a window of lengths.

relationships: The same average with a triangular weight, there for the Hilbert-Schmidt norm of the Gram form over a range of bandwidths, with the threshold 14.5 sqrt(m'/m_*)/g; here for a pointwise bound on prime sums at one height. Different statements; neither implies the other.
That proposition forces a large value at one length for a point rightmost by a margin; this one needs no margin but a separation in height and a window of lengths.

The conditional corollary on Turan's line; in the model this criterion replaces its small-constant zero count by a separation in height of the near-tied points, for a point rightmost in the whole configuration.
Part (4) is the second difference in the length of that lemma's part (1), under its premise.
The shell count of its part (2) is reused for the points below the margin.
